messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT: Okta /introspect 5xx rate spike detected — 502 responses 28% over last 5m across prod-edge-us-east. Paging on-call. :rotating_light:
Jamie: on it. seeing auth proxy errors piling up in prod logs. grabbing request ids.
Ravi: confirmed — token verification failing downstream, clients see 401s after our retry attempts exhaust. sample log:```
[auth-proxy] 2026-03-15T02:12:14Z req=abc123 okta.introspect 502 Bad Gateway
[auth-proxy] 2026-03-15T02:12:15Z req=abc124 retry=1 status=502
[auth-proxy] 2026-03-15T02:12:17Z req=abc124 final status=401 downstream
```
Sara: rough scope? how many customers affected?
Ravi: quick numbers from telemetry: ~18% of console login attempts failed (US-EAST), ~9% of token-verify calls returned 5xx then converted to 401 by our auth flow. Impact concentrated on interactive flows.
Alex: do we have a safe mitigation to reduce customer-visible failures? maybe treat 502 as transient and extend retry/backoff or serve from prefix cache for recent tokens.
Jamie: i can flip the introspect fallback flag on the auth-proxy to prefer cached session verification for 60s window. doing a quick config change in staging then prod.
ops-bot: runbook step: toggle feature flag AUTH_INTROSPECT_FALLBACK -> true via config-service. Command:```
curl -XPOST https://config.internal/v1/flags -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"key":"AUTH_INTROSPECT_FALLBACK","value":"true","env":"prod"}'
```
Jamie: deploying change now, will push to 10% canary -> 100% if metrics look good.
incidents-bot: status update: change applied to canary (10% prod). watch auth.introspect.502_rate and console.login.fail_rate.
Ravi: after canary, console login failure drops to ~6% on canary hosts. looks promising. escalate rollout.
Jamie: rolling out to 100% across prod-edge-us-east.
ops-bot: rollout complete. enabling extra retries and bumping timeout for introspect to 5s.
Sara: pinging support/sales slack to prep comms — likely some customers will see transient login errors.
Jamie: opened Okta ticket from our side: https://support.okta.com/incidents/78912 — they acknowledge degraded introspect in us-east-1. copying contact.
Alex: note for on-call: we should also enable token-cache read-only mode for any long-poll UI routes to avoid forcing fresh introspect calls. config snippet:```
# auth-proxy config
introspect:
  timeout_ms: 5000
  retries: 3
  fallback_cache_ttl_s: 60
  treat_502_as_transient: true
```
Ravi: metrics after full rollout: introspect 502 rate back to ~1.2% from 28%, console login failures down to baseline ~1.5%. 401 errors reduced by ~85%.
Maria: thanks team. i'll take the handoff for the night. will monitor Okta incident and consumer error ratios.
Jamie: handing off — checklist in thread pinned. actions for night oncall: 1) monitor auth.introspect.502_rate 2) check status.okta.com and ticket updates 3) be ready to roll back fallback if we see incorrect auth acceptance 4) prepare status page update if customers ask.
Maria: ack. putting a follow-up alert rule to email on >5% 5xx for 10m.
incidents-bot: incident severity lowered to SEV-3 — mitigation in place, third-party ongoing.
Sara: preparing short customer note for status.redwoood.com (draft in #marketing-ops). will hold until we confirm Okta's timeline.
Alex: quick safety check: we verified no tokens were incorrectly validated from cache? Ravi: ran sampling — cache reads correlated with prior successful introspect within TTL, no mismatches so far.
Jamie: postmortem owners: Jamie (mitigation), Ravi (metrics + QA), Maria (oncall summary). will schedule RCA tomorrow.
Maria: added follow-up tasks to the incidents board and will update thread if Okta posts resolution. :white_check_mark:
